conditions.rule: In the slaver-city's pits the lowest are made to rise — lowest base power wins the duel. Abilities that add power are traps.
Darwin's fortress permits no escape — Withdraw is locked. Once you confirm your selection you must commit. The only exit is losing.
On the homeland's hard ground tricks fail and only strength counts — no card abilities activate this turn. Raw power only, no on-commit or resolution effects.
In Darwin's menagerie specimens are shuffled on a whim — after commit, each player's card is replaced by a random card from their hand. You commit a sacrifice, not a fighter.
Storms break over the peaks without warning — +6 power strikes one randomly selected committed card after both are locked in.
Nothing stays hidden in the capital's open court — the opponent's card identity is revealed before you commit. They see yours in turn.
Where two legends once destroyed each other, legacy decides — if power is tied after all effects, the card with more career kills wins. Zero-kill cards lose all ties.
Skarrow Hold tests restraint, not strength — the higher-base-power card takes −5 power (to a minimum of 1). The mountain humbles the mighty.
In the illusion-warped village nothing is itself — each committed card's power becomes equal to the opponent's committed base power.
In the void identity falls away — if a unit's base power is lower than its kill count, that card's power becomes its career kills.
Experience favors the underdog — the weaker card gains +1 power for every 5 kills on its record, capped at +15.
Cards with zero kills fight with everything to prove — 0-kill cards gain +10.
Flawless records are exalted — Pristine (0 deaths, 1+ kill) cards gain +5.
The spotless are hunted — Pristine (0 deaths, 1+ kill) cards suffer −5.
Every scar is a weakness — each card loses 1 power per 2 deaths on its record.
Scars fuel fury — each card gains +1 power per death on its record, capped at +15.
The lesser rises — the lower base-power card gains +3.
Pedigree wins — the rarer card gains +3.
The low-born rise up — the lower-rarity card gains +5.
When base powers differ by 10 or more, the weaker card fells the giant outright.
Fortune tips the scales — each card gains a random +5 to +10.
The trailing side surges — whoever is behind in the match gains +3.
Experience tells — +1 power per 4 duels fought (kills + deaths), capped at +15.
Both blades cut true — both players' conjured units gain +5 power.
A stage for the great — Apex cards gain +2, all others suffer −2.
The grizzled fight hardest — cards with 3 or more deaths gain +2.
Endurance is rewarded — the card with fewer deaths gains +3.
The deep reflects only what a card is worth — each card's power becomes its own Charge cost ×10.
The banners call fresh blood to the line — both players draw 1 card when this ground is revealed.
The tide gives and takes — both players draw 2 cards, then discard 2 to the banish pile.
The beasts tolerate no aid — both players draw 1 card, then both players' support zones are locked for the duel.

Every bloodline answers to another — Amageras's Blessing overwhelms Omitsuki's Path, Omitsuki's Path overwhelms Kitanoo's Hunt, and Kitanoo's Hunt overwhelms Amageras's Blessing in turn. Whoever's camp beats the other's gets +6 power. Same camp on both sides means no swing.

ascStory.title: Placement
ascStory.beat: The corps yard sorts you before you've thrown a punch — high-family boys on one side, levy sons like you on the other. Sergeant Ossian Drell has broken cadets in this yard for thirty years; his right hand ends at the wrist in a fitted iron cap, and he doesn't raise it to call the pairings. "Kel'rua," he says. "Vench." Fenrik Vench is a causeway-lord's son who has never once been paired against someone beneath him — and he intends to keep it that way.

ascStory.title: The Instructor's Test
ascStory.beat: You lost the spar the whole yard saw. Drell watched a different fight — the one in your head, where you'd already won three moves before your body caught up. "Being clever is a locked door with your name filed off," he told you after, quiet enough that only you heard it. Today he doesn't send another cadet. Thirty years breaking recruits in this yard, and Sergeant Ossian Drell steps onto the sand himself — to find out exactly how far that locked door goes.

ascStory.title: What the Corps Won't Forgive
ascStory.beat: Word travels faster than any of you did. Something cracked loose in you during the Measure — a green pulse the whole city felt — and Darwin's Writ-officers don't need to understand what it was to know it's worth a body brought in alive. They find you at the gate, lacquered black and unhurried, the way men move when they've never once lost a chase. Whatever Tosa was to you, it isn't safe to be from here anymore.

ascStory.title: Animal Shelter
ascStory.beat: The fire is barely embers when he steps out of the dark like he was always standing there. Darwin sent him with two words and a name — bring me his head, or his hope — and Uso Oso has never once come back empty-handed. Steel finds him and doesn't seem to mind. "Sharp," he says, almost gentle. "But not deep." He isn't here to talk. He isn't sure, yet, that he wants to win.

ascStoryCh2.title: Sorn-Vallis
ascStoryCh2.beat: The gates close behind you before you understand you've walked through them. Sorn-Vallis flies no banner you'd recognize, but every corner of it answers to one woman. Veronica doesn't ask what you are — she takes one look and already knows exactly what's useful about you, the same way she takes everything else that crosses her city: quietly, completely, and as if it were always hers to begin with.

ascStoryCh2.title: Smokescreen
ascStoryCh2.beat: The festival crowd doesn't know it's watching a punishment. Somewhere below the stands they've dragged Uso Oso into the sand against a boy who can't be older than thirteen, and told him to make it a show. He won't. "Don't let them carve you hollow," he tells the boy instead, low enough that only the boy hears it. "Stay you. That's the fight they can't win." On the balcony above, something in a woman's smile stops being a woman's smile at all — and on the rooftop over all of it, Lagertha is already changing shape. You have to reach them before either finishes what it started.

ascStoryCh2.title: Queen Crimson
ascStoryCh2.beat: Whatever wore Ella Ballora's smile a moment ago doesn't bother wearing it now. What unfolds in the throne room beneath the arena is what she always was underneath — and it takes everything you have just to find the seam in her, a single ruby weak point Uso finally rips free with his bare hands. Dying, she offers you exactly what you came for: Darwin's stronghold, named aloud, yours for the taking if you let her live one minute longer. Lagertha, still wearing the wolf, doesn't wait for you to decide. The intel dies with her. Somewhere behind you, word is already reaching Keawe's sister — Kianna has just enlisted, fast-tracked into an elite unit they're calling the Black Wings.
